translations.literal: He then spent the whole night preparing two thousand horse troughs.
translations.idiomatic: That night he had two thousand horse troughs prepared.

sentences.zh: 周人聞之，以為大軍將至，乃解圍去。

translations.literal: When the Zhou heard of it they thought a great army was coming and lifted the siege and left.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou heard of it, assumed a great army was near, and lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 永業進位開府，封臨川王。

translations.literal: Yongye was promoted to Grand Prefect and enfeoffed as Prince of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yongye was promoted to grand prefect and enfeoffed as Prince of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 有甲士三萬，初聞晉州敗，請出兵北討，奏寢不報，永業慨憤。

translations.literal: He had thirty thousand armored troops; when he first heard of the defeat at Jinyang he requested to march north to attack, but his memorials slept unanswered and Yongye grew indignant.
translations.idiomatic: He had thirty thousand armored men. At the first news of Jinyang's fall he asked to march north; his memorials went unanswered, and Yongye burned with indignation.

sentences.zh: 又聞幷州亦陷，為周將常山公所逼，乃使其子須達告降於周。

translations.literal: When he also heard that Bingzhou had fallen and was pressed by the Zhou general Duke of Changshan, he sent his son Xuda to offer surrender to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Bingzhou fell too and the Zhou general Duke of Changshan pressed him, he sent his son Xuda to surrender to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 周武授永業上柱國。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou granted Yongye the rank Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou made Yongye pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 宣政末，出為襄州總管。

translations.literal: Late in Xuanzheng he went out as chief administrator of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xuanzheng he was sent out as chief administrator of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 大象二年，為行軍總管崔彥睦所殺。

translations.literal: In Elephant year 2 he was killed by campaigning general-in-chief Cui Yanmin.
translations.idiomatic: In Elephant year 2 he was killed by campaigning general-in-chief Cui Yanmin.

sentences.zh: 傅伏，太安人也。

translations.literal: Fu Fu was a man of Tai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Fu came from Tai'an.

sentences.zh: 父元興，儀同、北蔚州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yuanying was Grand Master of Splendid Parallels and Governor of Northern Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuanying was grand master of splendid parallels and governor of northern Yu province.

sentences.zh: 伏少從戎，以戰功稍至開府、永橋領民大都督。

translations.literal: Fu joined the army young and, through battle merit, gradually rose to Grand Prefect and chief of the Yongqiao tribal settlement.
translations.idiomatic: Fu took the army young and rose by battle merit to grand prefect and chief of the Yongqiao tribal settlement.

sentences.zh: 周帝前攻河陰，伏自橋夜渡，入守中潬城。

translations.literal: When the Zhou emperor advanced on Heyin, Fu crossed the bridge by night and entered to hold Zhongtan fortress.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou emperor advanced on Heyin, Fu crossed the bridge at night and entered Zhongtan fortress to hold it.

sentences.zh: 南城陷，被圍二旬不下。

translations.literal: The south city fell, but he was besieged for twenty days and did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: The south city fell, yet he held under siege for twenty days without yielding.

sentences.zh: 救兵至，周師還，伏謂行臺乞伏貴和曰：「賊已疲弊，願得精騎二千追擊之，可捷也。

translations.literal: When relief arrived the Zhou army withdrew; Fu said to circuit commissioner Qifu Guihe: "The enemy is worn out—I ask for two thousand elite cavalry to pursue them; victory is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Relief came and the Zhou withdrew. Fu told circuit commissioner Qifu Guihe, "The enemy is spent. Give me two thousand elite cavalry to pursue, and the victory is ours."

sentences.zh: 」貴和弗許。

translations.literal: Guihe would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Guihe refused.

sentences.zh: 武平六年，除東雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In Wuping year 6 he was made Governor of Eastern Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuping year 6 he was made governor of eastern Yong province.

sentences.zh: 會周兵來逼，伏出戰，卻之。

translations.literal: When Zhou troops pressed close he went out to fight and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou troops pressed in he fought them off.

sentences.zh: 周剋晉州，執獲行臺尉相貴，以之招伏，伏不從。

translations.literal: The Zhou took Jinyang and captured circuit commissioner Wei Xianggui, using him to summon Fu, but Fu would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou took Jinyang and captured circuit commissioner Wei Xianggui, whom they sent to summon Fu; Fu refused.

sentences.zh: 後主親救晉州，以伏為行臺右僕射。

translations.literal: The Later Sovereign personally went to relieve Jinyang and made Fu right vice minister of the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Sovereign marched in person to relieve Jinyang and made Fu right vice minister of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 周軍來掠，伏擊走之。

translations.literal: When Zhou troops came to raid he struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou raiders came he struck and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 周克幷州，遣韋孝寬與其子世寬來招伏曰：「幷州已平，故遣公兒來報，便宜急下。

translations.literal: The Zhou took Bingzhou and sent Wei Xiaokuan with his son Shikuan to summon Fu, saying: "Bingzhou is already pacified, so we send your son to report—submit at once."
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou took Bingzhou and sent Wei Xiaokuan with his son Shikuan to summon Fu: "Bingzhou is pacified. We send your son with the news—submit now."

sentences.zh: 」授上大將軍、武鄉郡開國公，即給告身，以金馬瑙二酒鐘為信。

translations.literal: They offered him Grand General and Duke of Wuxiang with an open state, gave him the patent on the spot, and sent two gold-and-agate wine vessels as tokens.
translations.idiomatic: They offered him grand general and Duke of Wuxiang with an open state, handed him the patent at once, and sent two gold-and-agate wine vessels as tokens of faith.

sentences.zh: 伏不受，謂孝寬曰：「事君有死無貳，此兒為臣不能竭忠，為子不能盡孝，人所讐疾，願即斬之，以號令天下。」

translations.literal: Fu would not accept and said to Xiaokuan: "To serve one's lord one has death but no second loyalty. This boy cannot exhaust loyalty as a subject or filial piety as a son—men loathe him. I ask that you cut off his head at once to proclaim it to the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Fu refused and told Xiaokuan, "A subject owes his lord death, not divided loyalty. This boy is no loyal subject and no filial son—men despise him. Cut off his head now and proclaim it to the realm."

sentences.zh: 周帝自鄴還至晉州，遣高阿那肱等百餘人臨汾召伏。

translations.literal: The Zhou emperor returned from Ye to Jinyang and sent Gao Anaigong and more than a hundred others to the Fen River to summon Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor returned from Ye to Jinyang and sent Gao Anaigong and more than a hundred men to the Fen to summon Fu.

sentences.zh: 伏出軍隔水相見，問至尊今在何處。

translations.literal: Fu led his army out and, across the water, asked where His Majesty was now.
translations.idiomatic: Fu marched out, met them across the water, and asked where His Majesty was.

sentences.zh: 阿那肱曰：「已被捉獲，別路入關。

translations.literal: Anaigong said: "He has already been captured and is entering the passes by another route."
translations.idiomatic: Anaigong said, "He is already captured and entering the passes by another road."

sentences.zh: 」伏仰天大哭，率衆入城，於聽事前北面哀號良久，然後降。

translations.literal: Fu looked up to heaven and wept loudly, led his troops into the city, and before the audience hall faced north and wailed for a long time before he submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Fu looked up and wept aloud, led his men into the city, and before the audience hall faced north and wailed a long while before he submitted.

sentences.zh: 周帝見之曰：「何不早下？

translations.literal: When the Zhou emperor saw him he said: "Why did you not submit sooner?"
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor saw him and said, "Why did you not submit sooner?"

sentences.zh: 」伏流涕而對曰：「臣三世蒙齊家衣食，被任如此，革命不能自死，羞見天地。

translations.literal: Fu wept as he answered: "For three generations my house has eaten Qi grain and been entrusted as I was; I could not die in the revolution—I am ashamed to face heaven and earth."
translations.idiomatic: Fu answered through tears, "Three generations of my house ate Qi grain and were trusted as I was. I could not die in the revolution—I am ashamed to face heaven and earth."

sentences.zh: 」周帝親執其手曰：「為臣當若此。

translations.literal: The Zhou emperor personally took his hand and said: "A subject should be like this."
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor took his hand and said, "This is how a subject should be."

sentences.zh: 朕平齊國，唯見公一人。

translations.literal: "In pacifying Qi I have seen only you."
translations.idiomatic: "In pacifying Qi I have seen only you."

sentences.zh: 」乃自食一羊肋，以骨賜伏，曰：「骨親肉疏，所以相付。

translations.literal: He himself ate a lamb rib and gave Fu the bone, saying: "Bone is kin to kin; flesh is distant—that is why I give this to you."
translations.idiomatic: He ate a lamb rib himself and gave Fu the bone, saying, "Bone is kin to kin; flesh is distant—that is why I entrust this to you."

sentences.zh: 」遂別引之與同食，令於侍伯邑宿衛，授上儀同，勑之曰：「若即與公高官，恐歸投者心動，努力好行，無慮不富貴。

translations.literal: He then led Fu aside to eat with him, had him lodge with the attendant guard, granted him Grand Master of Splendid Parallels, and charged him: "If I at once give you high office I fear those who come over will waver—work hard and have no fear of wealth and honor."
translations.idiomatic: He drew Fu aside to eat with him, lodged him with the attendant guard, made him grand master of splendid parallels, and charged him, "If I give you high rank at once, those who surrender will waver. Serve well—you will not lack wealth or honor."

sentences.zh: 」又問前救河陰得何官職。

translations.literal: He also asked what office he had received for saving Heyin before.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked what office Fu had received for holding Heyin before.

sentences.zh: 伏曰：「蒙一轉，授特進，永昌郡開國公。

translations.literal: Fu said: "I received one promotion—Special Advancement and Duke of Yongchang with an open state."
translations.idiomatic: Fu said, "One promotion—special advancement and Duke of Yongchang with an open state."

sentences.zh: 」周帝謂後主曰：「朕前三年教習兵馬，決意往取河陰，正為傅伏能守，城不可動，是以收軍而退。

translations.literal: The Zhou emperor said to the Later Sovereign: "Three years ago I trained troops and resolved to take Heyin, but because Fu Fu could hold it the city would not move, so I withdrew the army."
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor told the Later Sovereign, "Three years ago I drilled troops and meant to take Heyin, but Fu Fu held the city and it would not budge, so I withdrew."

sentences.zh: 公當時賞授何其薄也。

translations.literal: "Your rewards then were how meager!"
translations.idiomatic: "Your reward then was how meager!"

sentences.zh: 」賜伏金酒卮。

translations.literal: He gave Fu a gold wine cup.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Fu a gold wine cup.

sentences.zh: 後以為岷州刺史，尋卒。

translations.literal: Later he was made Governor of Minzhou and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made governor of Minzhou and soon died.

sentences.zh: 齊軍晉州敗後，兵將罕有全節者。

translations.literal: After the Qi army's defeat at Jinyang, few commanders and generals kept their integrity whole.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qi defeat at Jinyang, few officers kept their honor intact.

sentences.zh: 其殺身成仁者，有儀同叱干茍生，鎮南兗州，周帝破鄴，赦書至，茍生自縊死。

translations.literal: Among those who died to perfect loyalty was Grand Master of Splendid Parallels Chigan Gousheng, who garrisoned southern Yan Province; when the Zhou emperor took Ye and the amnesty arrived, Gousheng hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who died to perfect loyalty was grand master of splendid parallels Chigan Gousheng, garrisoning southern Yan province. When the Zhou took Ye and the amnesty arrived, Gousheng hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 又有開府、中侍中宦者田敬宣，本字鵬，蠻人也。

translations.literal: There was also Grand Prefect and Palace Attendant eunuch Tian Jingxuan, original name Peng, a barbarian.
translations.idiomatic: There was also grand prefect and palace attendant eunuch Tian Jingxuan, originally named Peng, a barbarian.

sentences.zh: 年十四五，便好讀書。

translations.literal: At fourteen or fifteen he loved reading.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen or fifteen he loved books.

sentences.zh: 既為閽寺，伺隙便周章詢請，每至文林館，氣喘汗流，問書之外，不暇他語。

translations.literal: Once in the palace service he seized every chance to inquire urgently; each time he reached the Hall of Forested Literature he would gasp and sweat, and beyond asking about books he had no leisure for other talk.
translations.idiomatic: Once in palace service he seized every chance to study. Each visit to the Hall of Forested Literature left him gasping and drenched in sweat; beyond books he had no time for anything else.

sentences.zh: 及視古人節義事，未嘗不感激沈吟。

translations.literal: When he read of ancient men's integrity he never failed to be moved and linger over it.
translations.idiomatic: When he read of ancient integrity he was always moved to long reflection.

sentences.zh: 顏之推重其勤學，甚加開獎，後遂通顯。

translations.literal: Yan Zhitui prized his diligence in study and greatly encouraged him; he later rose to prominence.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhitui prized his diligence and encouraged him generously; he later rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 後主之奔青州，遣其西出，參伺動靜，為周軍所獲。

translations.literal: When the Later Sovereign fled to Qingzhou he sent Jingxuan west to observe movements and was captured by Zhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Sovereign fled to Qingzhou he sent Jingxuan west to watch the enemy and was taken by Zhou troops.

sentences.zh: 問齊主何在，紿云已去。

translations.literal: Asked where the Qi sovereign was, he lied that he had already gone.
translations.idiomatic: Asked where the Qi sovereign was, he lied that the emperor had already gone.

sentences.zh: 毆捶服之，每折一支，辭色愈厲，竟斷四體而卒。

translations.literal: They beat him until he confessed; with each limb broken his words and color grew fiercer, and in the end all four limbs were broken off and he died.
translations.idiomatic: They beat him to make him confess; with each limb broken his voice and bearing grew fiercer, until all four were severed and he died.

sentences.zh: 又有雷顯和，晉州敗後，為建州道行臺左僕射。

translations.literal: There was also Lei Xianhe, who after the defeat at Jinyang became left vice minister of the Jianzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Lei Xianhe, who after Jinyang's fall became left vice minister of the Jianzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 周帝使其子招焉，顯和禁其子而不受。

translations.literal: The Zhou emperor had his son summon him, but Xianhe restrained his son and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor sent his son to summon him; Xianhe restrained his son and refused.

sentences.zh: 聞鄴城敗，乃降。

translations.literal: When he heard that Ye had fallen he submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Ye had fallen he submitted.

sentences.zh: 後主失幷州，使開府紇奚永安告急於突厥他缽略可汗。

translations.literal: After the Later Sovereign lost Bingzhou he sent Grand Prefect Hexi Yong'an to urge emergency aid on the Türk qaghan Tabo.
translations.idiomatic: After the Later Sovereign lost Bingzhou he sent grand prefect Hexi Yong'an to beg emergency aid of the Türk qaghan Tabo.

sentences.zh: 及聞齊滅，他缽處永安於吐谷渾使下。

translations.literal: When he heard that Qi had perished, Tabo placed Yong'an under a Tuyuhun envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Qi had perished, Tabo placed Yong'an under a Tuyuhun envoy.

sentences.zh: 永安抗言曰：「本國既敗，永安豈惜賤命！

translations.literal: Yong'an spoke boldly: "Our state is already defeated—would Yong'an spare a worthless life!"
translations.idiomatic: Yong'an spoke boldly: "Our state is already defeated—would I spare a worthless life!"

sentences.zh: 欲閉氣自絕，恐天下不知大齊有死節臣，唯乞一刀，以顯示遠近。

translations.literal: "I wished to hold my breath and end myself, but feared the realm would not know that Great Qi had a subject who died for principle—I ask only for one blade to show the distant and near."
translations.idiomatic: "I meant to hold my breath and die, but feared the world would not know Great Qi had a subject who died on principle. Give me one blade to show far and near."

sentences.zh: 」他缽嘉其壯烈，贈馬七十匹而歸。

translations.literal: Tabo admired his fierce loyalty, gave him seventy horses, and sent him home.
translations.idiomatic: Tabo admired his courage, gave him seventy horses, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 高保寧，代人也，不知其所從來。

translations.literal: Gao Baoning, a man of Dai, of unknown origin.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Baoning came from Dai; his origins are unknown.

sentences.zh: 武平末，為營州刺史，鎮黃龍，夷夏重其威信。

translations.literal: Late in Wuping he was Governor of Ying Province, garrisoning Huanglong; barbarians and Chinese alike respected his prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wuping he was governor of Ying province, garrisoning Huanglong; barbarians and Chinese alike respected his authority.

sentences.zh: 周師將至鄴，幽州行臺潘子晃下黃龍兵，保寧率驍銳並契丹、靺羯萬餘騎將赴救。

translations.literal: As Zhou troops were about to reach Ye, Youzhou circuit commissioner Pan Zihuang led Huanglong troops down; Baoning led elite cavalry together with Khitan and Mohe—more than ten thousand horsemen—to march to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhou troops neared Ye, Youzhou circuit commissioner Pan Zihuang led Huanglong troops down. Baoning led elite cavalry with Khitan and Mohe—more than ten thousand horsemen—to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 至北平，知子晃已發薊，又聞鄴都不守，便歸營。

translations.literal: Reaching Beiping he learned Zihuang had already set out from Ji and also heard that the capital Ye was lost, and returned to camp.
translations.idiomatic: At Beiping he learned Zihuang had already marched from Ji and that Ye had fallen; he turned back to camp.

sentences.zh: 周帝遣使招慰，不受勑書。

translations.literal: The Zhou emperor sent envoys to summon and reassure him; he would not accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor sent envoys to reassure him; he would not accept the edict.

sentences.zh: 范陽王紹義在突厥中，上表勸進，范陽署保寧為丞相。

translations.literal: Prince of Fanyang Shaoyi was among the Türks and submitted a memorial urging accession; Fanyang appointed Baoning chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Fanyang Shaoyi was with the Türks and submitted a memorial urging accession; Fanyang appointed Baoning chancellor.

sentences.zh: 及盧昌期據范陽城起兵，保寧引紹義集夷夏兵數萬騎來救之。

translations.literal: When Lu Changqi held Fanyang city and rose in arms, Baoning brought Shaoyi to gather barbarian and Chinese troops—tens of thousands of horsemen—to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Changqi seized Fanyang and rose in arms, Baoning brought Shaoyi to gather tens of thousands of barbarian and Chinese horsemen to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 至潞河，知周將宇文神舉已屠范陽，還據黃龍，竟不臣周。

translations.literal: Reaching the Lu River he learned the Zhou general Yuwen Shenju had already slaughtered Fanyang; he returned to hold Huanglong and in the end would not serve Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the Lu River he learned Zhou general Yuwen Shenju had already sacked Fanyang. He withdrew to hold Huanglong and never submitted to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：皮景和等爰自霸基，策名戎幕，間關夷險，迄於末運，位高任重，咸遂本誠，亦各遇其時也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Pi Jinghe and the others came from the hegemonic foundation, enrolled their names in the military camp, passed through hardship and peril to the final age, held high rank and heavy responsibility, and all fulfilled their original loyalty—each also met his time.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Pi Jinghe and the others rose from the hegemonic foundation, took their names into the war camp, passed through hardship to the dynasty's end, held high rank and heavy trust, and each kept faith to the end—they too met their hour.

sentences.zh: 傅伏之徒，俱表忠節，不然則丹青簡冊安可貴乎？

translations.literal: Men of Fu Fu's company—all displayed loyalty and constancy; otherwise how could painted likenesses and written registers be held precious?
translations.idiomatic: Fu Fu and men like him all kept faith to the last; without such souls, of what worth would painted likenesses in the halls of fame, or their names in the annals, ever be?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：唯此諸將，榮名是保，不愆不忘，以斯終老。

translations.literal: Appraisal: These generals alone preserved their honored names—without lapse, without forgetting—and so ended their days.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: Only these generals kept their honored names unstained—no lapse, no forgetting—and lived out their days in that same steadfastness.

sentences.zh: 傅子之輩，逢茲不造，未遇烈風，誰知勁草。

translations.literal: Fu's sons and their like met this ill-starred hour; before the fierce wind blew, who could tell the tough grass?
translations.idiomatic: Fu Fu's sons and men like them met an hour out of joint; before the gale came, who could tell which blade of grass would stand unbowed?
